acceptance_checks.description: ow_tp_demo.files holds exactly 10000 documents for ns=demo, recomputed from Atlas
Order-independent md5 over the migrated file-metadata line format equals manifest checksum db614663b2c6d41141cae82261b416d5
The DynamoDB ns attribute is carried onto every document as the tenant field; no document is written without it
DynamoDB numeric attributes become BSON numbers and byte/binary attributes become BSON binary; nothing is stringified
The 40 items whose s3_key has no backing object are reported by item key and are migrated with an explicit orphan marker rather than dropped
A second migration run leaves counts, checksums and the reported orphan set byte-identical

planted_anomalies.description: 40 file-metadata items point at an s3_key with no backing object; they must be detected and marked, never silently dropped or repaired
1 missing hourly S3 event partition under data-lake/events/demo/
planted_anomalies.reason: The S3 event lake is the Databricks track's source; no MongoDB unit ingests hourly event objects, so this anomaly is out of scope for the Atlas migration and is not reported by any Mongo recon.

encoding_policy.input_encoding: UTF-8 as returned by the DynamoDB API through boto3
encoding_policy.byte_transparency: Attribute values are carried through unchanged; binary attributes are stored as BSON binary with their original bytes
encoding_policy.invalid_bytes: An attribute that cannot be decoded is quarantined with the raw bytes hex-encoded; it is never replaced by a lossy substitute character

malformed_record_policy.details: Unexpected extra attributes are tolerated and carried through under an explicit extras subdocument, attributed in the recon report. An item missing its partition key, ns, or s3_key fails into quarantine; a missing value may never fail open into an empty string.

empty_input_semantics.details: A scan that returns zero items leaves prior Atlas output untouched and exits non-zero; an empty scan at demo scale is a source-connectivity failure.
